🧠 CORTEX

A self-supervising learning layer that preflights any pipeline, then re-optimizes it — and keeps learning.
Drop it into an existing repo. It maps what you run, finds where it leaks, and improves it on a schedule — with health-gates so it never "succeeds" while doing nothing.

preflight · supervised RL · recursive learning · pid-safe orchestration · $0 to run

--- ## Why CORTEX exists Most automation stacks rot silently. A nightly job exits `0`, a dashboard stays green, and yet nothing is actually learning or improving — a stale lock, an empty reward signal, a drifted config. Nobody notices for days because *"exited cleanly"* was mistaken for *"did the work."* CORTEX is the missing **supervisor**: a layer that runs your learning/optimization work as **health-gated steps**, verifies each one produced *real* output, and refuses to report success on a no-op. It ships with a **preflight** that inspects a pipeline it's never seen before and tells you — before it touches anything — what it found, what's underperforming, and what it would improve. > **One-liner:** *CORTEX is a conductor for your automation's brain. It preflights, optimizes, and > self-audits — so "green" means "genuinely improving," not "ran without crashing."* --- ## What it does (three layers) | Layer | Role | Guarantee | |---|---|---| | **Preflight** | Scans a target repo/pipeline, detects systems & entry points, ranks optimization opportunities | Read-only. Never mutates. Produces a report you approve before anything runs. | | **Supervisor** | Runs learning/optimization steps (RL self-play, recursive learning, distillers) as gated children | Verifies real output per step; retries silent no-ops; alarms instead of exiting-0-on-nothing. | | **Optimizer** | Applies the preflight's approved improvements to *your* existing pipelines | Every mutation is gated, reversible, and logged. Nothing lands without a health check. | --- ## Modules — the bundle CORTEX is a **host with a module registry**. Each capability is a self-contained, white-labeled module that exposes a common contract (`preflight()`, `run()`, `verify()`) so the supervisor can schedule it, health-gate it, and feed its output back — without knowing its internals. You enable the ones your pipeline needs; the rest stay dormant. | Module | What it does | Health signal (what "produced output" means) | |---|---|---| | **self-play** | Multi-environment reinforcement learning (GRPO-style): propose variants → score → group-advantage → distill | new episodes + reward delta | | **recursive-learn** | Auto-detect signals → predict → act → score → reinforce → synthesize one learning, each cycle more informed | new cycle appended + surprises logged | | **flywheel** | Revenue/outcome flywheel: surface opportunities → trajectory → targets → re-optimize | new surfaced items + trajectory delta | | **distill** | Compresses the cycle's raw learnings into durable, reusable rules | learnings file grew | | **adoption** | Reads harvested learnings / knowledge-graphs / vectors and **ships them into the live pipeline** — a committed diff, routing/config/prompt change, retuned threshold | an **applied diff** landed (not just a ledger write) | | **sentience** | The always-on feedback layer that consumes learnings and updates the self-model | belief-updates written | > **The loop closes on an applied diff, not a ledger write.** CORTEX tracks an **adoption rate** — > learnings *applied* ÷ learnings *harvested*. A stack that harvests but never applies looks healthy > (green, growing ledgers) while nothing improves; a low adoption rate is itself an alarm. Each cycle, > the system should be measurably different — and able to point at what changed. > Modules are the point. The three layers below are the *frame* that makes any module safe to run; > the registry is where self-play RL, the flywheels, and recursive learning actually live. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Conductor["⏱️ Scheduler / Conductor (cron, CI, or megacycle)"] C[invoke cortex] end C --> PF["🔎 PREFLIGHT
detect systems · rank opportunities · report"] PF -->|approved plan| SUP subgraph SUP["🧠 CORTEX SUPERVISOR"] direction LR L1["step: self-play RL"] L2["step: recursive learning"] L3["step: distill / reoptimize"] end L1 --> HG{"health-gate
produced real output?"} L2 --> HG L3 --> HG HG -->|yes| LEDGER[("📒 runs + health ledger")] HG -->|silent no-op| RETRY["retry once → else ALARM"] RETRY --> LEDGER LEDGER --> FB["♻️ feedback: learnings feed the next run
(each cycle strictly more informed)"] FB -.-> SUP classDef gate fill:#3b1d5e,stroke:#a06bd6,color:#fff; class HG,RETRY gate; ``` **The invariant that makes it trustworthy:** every step is wrapped in a **pid-liveness lock** (not a naive age-only lock). A crashed run leaves a dead-PID corpse; an age-only lock treats that corpse as a "live run" and blocks all work until it ages out. CORTEX checks whether the holder is *actually alive* (`process.kill(pid, 0)`), so a dead run never wedges the pipeline. This one detail is the difference between a supervisor that self-heals and one that silently stalls. --- ## Quickstart ```bash # 1. Preflight — read-only, tells you what CORTEX sees and would do node scripts/cortex.js preflight --target /path/to/your/repo # 2. Run the supervised learning cycle (health-gated, safe writes only) node scripts/cortex.js run # 3. Apply approved optimizations to your pipeline (gated + reversible) node scripts/cortex.js optimize --plan .cortex/preflight-plan.json ``` Everything is **fail-open** and **$0** to run — CORTEX orchestrates whatever model/router you already use; it does not require a paid API of its own. --- ## Health-gating: the core idea A step is only "successful" if it produced **verifiable new output**: ``` step "self-play" → episodes_total increased ? → ✅ ok step "recursive" → new cycle appended to ledger ? → ✅ ok step "distill" → learnings file grew ? → ✅ ok → exit 0 but NOTHING new → ⚠️ silent no-op → retry → 🚨 alarm ``` The ledger (`.cortex/health.json`) records `status`, `lastRun`, `producedOutput`, and a human-readable `detail` per step — so "is my learning loop actually learning?" is a one-line answer, not an archaeology dig through logs. --- ## Repository layout ``` CORTEX/ ├── README.md ← you are here ├── lib/ │ └── pid-lock.js ← pid-liveness single-flight lock (the anti-wedge primitive) ├── scripts/ │ └── cortex.js ← preflight · run · optimize entrypoint ├── docs/ │ ├── architecture.md ← deep dive: conductor / supervisor / optimizer │ ├── preflight.md ← how detection + opportunity-ranking works │ └── health-gates.md ← the no-op-detection contract └── examples/ └── sample-pipeline/ ← a toy pipeline you can preflight in 30 seconds ``` --- ## Design principles 1. **Green must mean improving.** Exiting cleanly is not success; producing verified new learning is. 2. **Never wedge.** Locks check liveness, not just age. A dead run is reclaimed immediately. 3. **Read before write.** Preflight is always non-destructive; every mutation is gated and reversible. 4. **Each cycle strictly more informed.** Outputs feed back so the next run starts from what the last one learned. 5. **Portable & $0.** Bring your own router/models; CORTEX is the orchestration and the discipline, not a paywall. ---

the failure mode

Automation stacks rot silently.

A nightly job exits 0. The dashboard stays green. And yet nothing learned anything for three days — a stale lock, an empty reward signal, a drifted config. Nobody noticed, because "exited cleanly" got mistaken for "did the work."

A dead process left a lock behind. An age-only lock can't tell a working run from a corpse, so it blocked every new run until it aged out. The loop kept exiting 0 — doing nothing — while the metrics that would've caught it were never checked. CORTEX exists to close exactly this gap.
what it does

Three layers, one discipline.

Each layer is safe by construction — read before write, verify before report, reclaim before wedge.

01 / READ-ONLY

Preflight

Scans a target repo or pipeline, detects its systems and entry points, and ranks where the biggest optimization wins are — before touching a single file.

guarantee: never mutates. Produces a plan you approve.
02 / GATED

Supervisor

Runs your learning steps — self-play RL, recursive learning, distillers — as health-gated children. Verifies each produced real output; retries silent no-ops.

guarantee: alarms instead of exiting-0-on-nothing.
03 / REVERSIBLE

Optimizer

Applies the preflight's approved improvements back into your existing pipeline. Every mutation is gated, logged, and reversible — nothing lands without a check.

guarantee: rollback-safe. Health-checked on the way in.
architecture

Conductor → Supervisor → Feedback.

The scheduler invokes CORTEX. CORTEX runs each step behind a health-gate and a pid-liveness lock, writes the result to a ledger, and feeds the learnings back so the next cycle starts more informed.

the core contract

A step only "succeeds" if it produced new output.

CORTEX snapshots each step's output before and after. Exit 0 isn't enough — the ledger has to show something new, or the step is flagged, retried, and escalated.

quickstart

Three commands.

Preflight is read-only, so the first command is always safe to run against any repo.

# 1 · read-only — what CORTEX sees and would improve
node scripts/cortex.js preflight --target /path/to/your/repo

# 2 · run the supervised learning cycle (health-gated, safe writes)
node scripts/cortex.js run

# 3 · apply approved optimizations (gated + reversible)
node scripts/cortex.js optimize --plan .cortex/preflight-plan.json
design principles

Five rules it never breaks.

01

Green means improving

Exiting cleanly is not success. Producing verified new learning is.

02

Never wedge

Locks check liveness, not just age. A dead run is reclaimed immediately.

03

Read before write

Preflight is always non-destructive; every mutation is gated and reversible.

04

Each cycle more informed

Outputs feed back, so the next run starts from what the last one learned.

05

Portable & $0

Bring your own router and models. CORTEX is the orchestration and the discipline.
